46	
47	# WhosOnSet — Project Overview
48	
49	A React 18 + TypeScript + Firebase social/jobs platform for the film industry. Bundled with Webpack, deployed to Firebase Hosting + Cloud Functions + Firestore + Storage.
50	
51	## ⚠️ Before every local/manual build / fresh checkout
52	
53	The `.env` file is not in git. It must exist on disk at the repo root before a local/manual `npm run build`, otherwise `dotenv-webpack` injects `undefined` for all `REACT_APP_FIREBASE_*` keys and the built site dies with `auth/invalid-api-key`. GitHub Actions production deploys write `.env` from repository secrets before building.
54	
55	**Symptoms of a missing `.env`:**
56	- `dist/main.*.js` has no `AIzaSy...` string in it
57	- Deployed site throws `FirebaseError: Firebase: Error (auth/invalid-api-key)` on first load
58	
59	**Procedure for any fresh checkout / new worktree / new machine running local builds:**
60	1. Copy `.env` over from a working install, or rebuild it from `env-template.txt`.
61	2. Verify with `grep -c AIza dist/main.*.js` after `npm run build` — should print `1`, not `0`.
62	
63	**Incident 2026-05-14:** committing `git rm --cached .env` in a branch and then fast-forward merging it into `main` caused git to delete `.env` from `main`'s working tree (correct git behavior, since the file had been "tracked", became "deleted", and your local copy matched HEAD so git didn't preserve it). A subsequent prod deploy shipped a bundle with no API key. Resolution: copied `.env` back from the worktree, rebuilt, redeployed.
64	
65	## ⚠️ Data safety — read first
66	
67	This is a **live production site with real personal user data in Firestore**. The owner has stated explicitly that lost data is irrecoverable. Treat this as a hard guardrail:
68	
69	- **Never** run a destructive Firestore command (mass delete, schema migration, collection drop) without explicit, scoped approval *in the current conversation*.
70	- The two parallel project collections (`Projects/` capital P, `projects/` lowercase) are **both live with real readers** — see P0 #6 below. Treat both as untouchable until a proper migration plan is approved.
71	- Code-only changes (UI, services, build, docs, dead-code, route gating) are fair game without per-change approval — the guardrail is specifically about Firestore data.
72	- The existing JSON-dump backup scripts (`backup-firestore*.sh`, `scripts/backup-firestore-simple.cjs`) are **unsafe as a backup of record**: they only cover a hardcoded subset of collections and **miss `Projects/` capital-P, `jobPostings`, `blogPosts`, `directMessages`**, plus all subcollections. They are usable as ad-hoc snapshots but cannot be trusted to fully restore the database. Once the managed schedule below is set up, these should be archived or deleted.
73	
74	### Backup setup — done 2026-05-14
75	
76	Three layers of protection on the `my-film-jobs` Firestore `(default)` database, location `nam5`:
77	
78	| Layer | What it covers | Status |
79	|-------|----------------|--------|
80	| **PITR** (Point-in-Time Recovery) | Continuous restore to any second within the last 7 days. Recovers from accidental writes/deletes. | ✅ enabled (`pointInTimeRecoveryEnablement: POINT_IN_TIME_RECOVERY_ENABLED`) |
81	| **Weekly scheduled backups** | Server-side snapshot every Sunday, 14-week retention. Survives DB deletion. | ✅ scheduled (Sunday weekly recurrence, retention 8467200s) |
82	| **Delete protection** | Prevents the database itself from being dropped. | ✅ enabled (`deleteProtectionState: DELETE_PROTECTION_ENABLED`) |
83	
84	The setup ran via `scripts/setup-firestore-backups.sh` (idempotent — safe to re-run). The first weekly backup lands the next Sunday after 2026-05-14; PITR already covers everything up to right now.
85	
86	**Note about on-demand backups:** `gcloud firestore backups create` does not exist; on-demand snapshots aren't available in the managed-backups API. If you ever need an extra ad-hoc backup, options are (a) wait for the next Sunday scheduled run, (b) add a daily schedule temporarily, or (c) use the older `gcloud firestore export` to dump to a GCS bucket. For most data-loss scenarios, PITR is the answer.
87	
88	**To verify** later:
89	
90	```sh
91	gcloud firestore backups schedules list --database='(default)' --project=my-film-jobs
92	```
93	
94	**To trigger an on-demand backup** any time:
95	
96	```sh
97	gcloud firestore backups create --database='(default)' --project=my-film-jobs --retention=4w
98	```
99	
100	**To restore** from a backup (always restores to a NEW database, then you switch the app over — never in-place):
101	
102	```sh
103	gcloud firestore backups list --location=<region> --project=my-film-jobs
104	gcloud firestore databases restore \
105	    --source-backup=<backup-name> \
106	    --destination-database=<new-db-id> \
107	    --project=my-film-jobs
108	```

```text
527	    try {

530	      const snapshot = await uploadBytes(storageRef, file);
531	      const downloadURL = await getDownloadURL(snapshot.ref);

533	      // Create screenplay data with proper typing

536	        name: file.name,
537	        type: file.type || 'application/octet-stream',
538	        url: downloadURL,

540	        teamMembers: [currentUser.uid],
541	        size: file.size,
542	        uploadedAt: now,
543	        lastModified: now
544	      };

546	      // Save to Firestore

659	  const formatTimeAgo = (date: Date) => {
660	    const now = new Date();
661	    const diff = now.getTime() - date.getTime();
662	    const minutes = Math.floor(diff / 60000);
663	    const hours = Math.floor(diff / 3600000);
664	    const days = Math.floor(diff / 86400000);
665	
666	    if (minutes < 60) return `${minutes}m ago`;
667	    if (hours < 24) return `${hours}h ago`;
668	    return `${days}d ago`;
669	  };
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-27 12:52:11Z)**_

Plan written to [PROJECT_OVERVIEW.md](PROJECT_OVERVIEW.md) as a new top-level section dated 2026-05-27. Key points:

**Two workstreams, broken into discrete agent-pickup-able steps:**

- **A — Student → supervisor flow** (A1–A6): adds a `'supervisor'` role, fixes the existing bug where workspace creation never actually persists to Firestore, scopes screenplays to workspaces, tightens the `workspaces` Firestore rule, reuses the existing annotation infra for comments.
- **B — In-browser Fountain editor** (B1–B7): adds `format: 'pdf' | 'fountain'` + `fountainSource` to the existing `screenplays` collection (no new collection), single textarea + debounced last-write-wins save, live page count in the top-right via a Fountain element-aware heuristic (60-char action lines, 35-char dialogue, 55 lines per page).

**Important things I flagged for you to confirm before any agent runs step A4:**

1. **Existing workspace creation never wrote to Firestore** — `handleCreateWorkspace` only updates local state. So either there are zero real workspaces in prod, or there's a stash created via a different path. This decides whether step A4's stricter rule needs a backfill.
2. Whether the supervisor should see *all* a student's screenplays or only workspace-scoped ones (plan defaults to scoped — privacy-preserving).
3. Email notifications on comments — wanted or noisy?
4. Fountain → PDF export — defer or include?

Each step has acceptance criteria and a file cheat-sheet at the end so a future agent can pick up step N cold and know exactly what to touch.

- `supervisor` role is functionally identical to `member` for access, but every annotation they author gets a denormalized `supervisor: true` flag so a future "evaluation view" can filter "comments from the teacher" cheaply.

**New B3a section — toolbar + shortcuts:**
- Six toolbar buttons (Scene, Action, Character, Parenthetical, Dialog, Transition) each acting on the current line.
- **Scene button cycles `INT.` → `EXT.` → `INT./EXT.`** on repeated presses so it stays one button.
- **`Tab` cycles element types** (Action → Character → Dialog → Parenthetical → Transition → Scene → Action), Shift+Tab cycles backward — the prime shortcut, matching Final Draft/Highland muscle memory.
- Per-element shortcuts use **`Alt`/`Option`+letter** (S, A, C, P, D, T). Reason explained in the doc: `Cmd`/`Ctrl` combos conflict with browser features everywhere; `Alt`+letter is free *while a textarea is focused and we call `preventDefault`*. That's the "claim ownership during edit" you mentioned — it comes free with normal event handling, no special API needed.
- Buttons show the shortcut as a small chip (`Scene` / `⇥ ⌥S`), platform-aware (`⌥` on Mac, `Alt` on Windows/Linux).
- Active-element highlighting so the writer can see what mode the current line is in.
- Mutation logic lives as a pure function `applyElementType` in `src/utilities/fountain.ts` for unit testing.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-27 14:23:41Z)**_

Plan updated to reflect the corrected supervisor model:

**Supervisor permissions corrected:**
- `supervisor` = **read + comment + annotate, NO edit on any screenplay in the workspace** (including their own — if a teacher also wants to contribute, they toggle back to `member`).
- Enforced in **Firestore rules**, not just UI — A4 now spells out the `isEffectiveSupervisor()` rule helper that blocks `screenplays/{id}` writes from anyone effectively in supervisor mode. Annotations remain writable, so the separation is exactly "comment freely, never touch the work."

**Two paths to supervisor (new A1.5 section):**
1. **Owner-assigned**: workspace creator/admin tags someone as supervisor in the add/edit-member modal. Cannot be removed by the assignee — only the owner can revoke.
2. **Self-promotion (the Francisco path)**: any invited member whose `crewProfiles/{uid}.isTeacher === true` sees a "Act as supervisor" toggle on their own member card. Flipping it adds their uid to `workspaces/{id}.selfElectedSupervisors`. Non-teachers don't see the toggle. So students just add Francisco to the workspace as a normal member; he self-tags. No special student instructions needed.

**Schema additions captured:**
- `crewProfiles/{uid}.isTeacher: boolean` — surfaced on the user's own profile-edit page with a checkbox.
- `workspaces/{id}.supervisorIds: string[]` (owner-assigned, denormalized for rules).
- `workspaces/{id}.selfElectedSupervisors: string[]` (self-promoted, denormalized for rules).
- Screenplays get a denormalized `workspaceId` so the rule can resolve effective role.

**5 rules-playground acceptance tests** spelled out for each direction (member edits OK, supervisor edit denied, self-elected supervisor toggles back and edit succeeds, etc.) so the implementing agent can verify before deploying.

I also removed the question I was confused about — you're right that it's a non-issue: supervisors are always explicitly invited to a workspace, so "before they were invited" doesn't arise.

```text
  position: initial;

}

.textLayer .highlight.end {
  border-radius: 0 4px 4px 0;
}

.textLayer .highlight.middle {
  border-radius: 0;
}

.textLayer .highlight.selected {
  background-color: var(--highlight-selected-bg-color);
}

/* Avoids https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/issues/13840 in Chrome */
.textLayer br::selection {
  background: transparent;
}

.textLayer .endOfContent {

  position: absolute;
  inset: 100% 0 0;

  user-select: none;
}

  top: 0;
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-27 19:41:33Z)**_

Typecheck is clean. Here's what I found:

## Root cause of the "duplicate pages / dark grey unreadable" symptom

The symptom is a classic **react-pdf v10 missing-CSS** bug. When the project upgraded from react-pdf@5 → @10 (commit `48e2f46b`), it stopped getting `TextLayer.css` automatically — v5 bundled it, v10 requires explicit imports. Without `TextLayer.css`:

- The PDF canvas renders the text (correct, normal).
- The text layer renders the SAME text as `<span>` elements on top — but without the CSS rule `.textLayer :is(span, br) { color: transparent; ... }` (verified in `node_modules/react-pdf/dist/Page/TextLayer.css:51`), those spans display as **opaque dark text** in the browser default color, slightly off-pixel from the canvas glyphs.
- Visually: each page looks doubled, fuzzy, "dark grey almost unreadable." Exactly the symptom.

## Your current fix is correct

The uncommitted diff at [ScreenplayViewer.tsx:4-5](src/components/Collaboration/ScreenplayViewer.tsx) adds both required imports:

```ts
import 'react-pdf/dist/Page/AnnotationLayer.css';
import 'react-pdf/dist/Page/TextLayer.css';
```

These resolve to real files (verified in `node_modules/react-pdf/dist/Page/`), and importing them via webpack injects the rules globally. This should fully eliminate both the duplicated-text appearance and the dark-grey unreadability.

## Other defensive changes in your diff that look good

- **Worker URL**: switched from `cdnjs` (which doesn't host every `pdfjs-dist` patch release — that broke loading whenever the bundled version drifted) to `cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/pdfjs-dist@${pdfjs.version}/...` which serves the npm package directly. Much more reliable.
- **State reset on screenplay change**: `setError(null); setUseNativePdfFallback(false); setLoading(true); setNumPages(null)` in the `useEffect` keyed on `screenplay.id` — fixes a stale-state-bleed bug when you opened a new screenplay after the previous one failed.
- **12s fallback timer + native open-in-new-tab link**: graceful degradation if pdf.js can't load (e.g. Storage CORS not yet applied, network blip).
- **Removed `minHeight: 900` from `.page-container`** and centered via flex — the old fixed-minHeight on the inline style was almost certainly contributing to layout instability when windowing kicked in.

## Where I'd verify before declaring this done

The fix is correct in the code, but PDFs are rendered, not type-checked — you need eyes on a real PDF:

1. Open the site, open any uploaded PDF screenplay in the collaboration viewer.
2. Confirm text is sharp (single rendering on the canvas, no visible duplicate text overlay).
3. Confirm the gutter is the light slate (`#e5e7eb`) not dark grey.
4. Confirm scrolling reveals later pages without "ghost" duplicates.
5. Try selecting text on the page — selection should still work (proves the text layer is present, just transparent).

Want me to start the dev server and walk through the viewer with you?

You've already done substantial work on the plan I drafted: [CollaborationHub.tsx](src/components/Collaboration/CollaborationHub.tsx) +1246 lines, [firestore.rules](firestore.rules) +100 lines, [Collaboration.ts](src/types/Collaboration.ts) +24 lines. You've shipped real work. Let me give you a grounded read on what's there vs. what would make student-collaboration *great* rather than just functional, then ask where to go next.

## What's already in good shape

- **A1 + A2 + A3 + A4 from the plan are essentially done.** Workspaces persist (`addDoc` at [CollaborationHub.tsx:637](src/components/Collaboration/CollaborationHub.tsx:637)), `memberIds`/`supervisorIds`/`viewerIds` are kept in sync, screenplays carry `workspaceId`, and when members are added the screenplays' `teamMembers` array is fanned out via [`syncWorkspaceScreenplayAccess`](src/components/Collaboration/CollaborationHub.tsx:491).
- **Firestore rules are substantial and correct** — `canEditScreenplayData` + `keepsScreenplayOwnership` + the `isWorkspaceReadOnlyParticipant` check enforce no-edit-by-supervisor at the rules layer, not just UI. The `get` vs `list` split on workspaces is the right Firestore idiom for array-membership rules.
- **Beyond-plan win**: archive → soft-delete → 30-day recovery for workspaces. That's a meaningful trust feature.
- **Live updates inside the viewer**: [ScreenplayViewer.tsx](src/components/Collaboration/ScreenplayViewer.tsx) already uses `onSnapshot` on annotations/tags/sessions — so when the teacher comments, an open viewer reflects it without reload.
- **Teacher flag already exists in crew profiles** (used by [MyStudentsPage.tsx:64](src/pages/MyStudentsPage.tsx:64), [PublicCrewPage.tsx:80](src/pages/PublicCrewPage.tsx:80), [ProducerView.tsx:73](src/pages/ProducerView.tsx:73)) — no schema work needed for A1.5; just wire to CollaborationHub.

## What's missing for "great" — ordered by leverage

1. **Teacher self-promotion (plan A1.5) — not wired in CollaborationHub.** Zero references to `isTeacher` or `selfElectedSupervisors` in the hub. Without it, students still have to know to tag you as supervisor at invite time. This is the smallest change with the biggest ergonomic payoff: a "Act as supervisor" toggle on your own member card, visible only if your profile has `isTeacher === true`.

2. **The hub doesn't use `onSnapshot` — only the viewer does.** Workspaces and the screenplay list load via `getDocs` one-shot. Student uploads while teacher's page is open → teacher doesn't see it in the list until reload. Same for new comments — the *count* doesn't update live. For "great," the list itself needs to be live.

3. **No comment-count badge on each screenplay row.** Right now you have to open the viewer to know if there are open notes. A live count of unresolved annotations next to each screenplay name is the #1 "did the teacher leave feedback" signal.

4. **No annotation lifecycle (open / addressed / resolved).** The data model already has `resolved` (I saw it in viewer styles), but no UI to mark "I've addressed this" from the student side and no filter for "open notes from teacher." Without this loop closure, comments pile up and feel ignored.

5. **No activity feed in the workspace card.** "Francisco commented on Scene2.pdf · 3m ago" / "Maya uploaded Act1_revised.pdf · 1h ago". This is the single feature that makes a workspace *feel alive*. Backed by a thin `workspaceActivity` collection or a denormalized `recentActivity` array on the workspace doc.

6. **No notifications when the teacher comments.** A red-dot on the user menu + an optional email via the existing `functions/src/emailService.ts`. Students will check more often if they know something landed.

7. **Drag-and-drop multi-upload + better empty states.** The current screenplay-tab upload card is functional but feels like a form. Drag a PDF onto the workspace; show a friendly "Invite your teacher" prompt when the workspace is empty.

8. **No workspace-level chat / discussion thread.** Annotations are spatial (pinned to PDF regions). For general "hey Francisco, can you look at the climax?" messages, no surface exists. `RealTimeCollaboration.tsx` already exists but isn't wired in.

9. **Mobile.** Students mostly work on phones. ScreenplayViewer has a `@media (max-width: 900px)` block; CollaborationHub doesn't.

10. **Workstream B (Fountain editor) — not started.** Still on the plan, untouched.

## Where I'd start if you want this to feel great fast

The three changes that together flip the feel from "form-driven LMS" to "the teacher is in the room with me" are:

- **A1.5 self-tag** (small, unblocks your workflow)
- **`onSnapshot` on the hub** (small-medium, makes everything else feel live)
- **Comment-count badges + resolved/open status** (medium, closes the feedback loop)

Activity feed and notifications come right after.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-27 20:05:39Z)**_

G1 + G2 are done. Typecheck is clean.

## What changed

**G2 — Hub is now live:**
- [CollaborationHub.tsx:321](src/components/Collaboration/CollaborationHub.tsx:321) — workspaces use `onSnapshot` on `where('memberIds', 'array-contains', currentUser.uid)`. Selection survives across snapshots (matched by `id`), and falls back to first active when nothing's selected.
- [CollaborationHub.tsx:333](src/components/Collaboration/CollaborationHub.tsx:333) — screenplays use three parallel `onSnapshot` queries (`uploadedBy`, `teamMembers array-contains`, `workspaceId in [...]`), each maintaining a sub-map; results are merged client-side. Re-subscribes when accessible workspace IDs change (keyed on a sorted-joined string to avoid spurious tear-downs).
- Removed obsolete `loadWorkspaces` (~35 lines) and `loadUserScreenplays` (~65 lines) — and the manual refresh calls in `addUsersToWorkspace` and `handleDeleteScreenplay` that used to compensate for the lack of subscriptions.

**G1 — Teacher self-tag:**
- New state: `isTeacher`, `toggleSupervisorPending`.
- [CollaborationHub.tsx:386](src/components/Collaboration/CollaborationHub.tsx:386) — one-shot `getDoc` on `crewProfiles/{uid}` reads `isTeacher === true || profileType === 'teacher'` (parity with `MyStudentsPage`/`ProducerView`).
- Helpers: `isSelfElectedSupervisor`, `getEffectiveRole`, `canSelfElectSupervisor`, `toggleSelfElectedSupervisor` — the toggle writes `selfElectedSupervisors: arrayUnion(uid)` / `arrayRemove(uid)`.
- UI on each workspace card: a role chip ("You: member" / "You: supervisor (self)") plus, when eligible, an "Act as supervisor" / "Step down" button. Visible only when the user has a role in the workspace OR is a teacher with eligibility to self-elect. Owners cannot self-toggle (they're already in control).

**Firestore rules — narrow self-toggle allowance:**
- [firestore.rules:121](firestore.rules:121) — new helpers `profileIsTeacher(uid)` and `isSelfSupervisorToggle(workspaceData, requestData, uid)`. The latter requires: the caller is a member, not the owner, has the teacher flag, the diff *only* touches `selfElectedSupervisors` + `updatedAt`, and the change is symmetric in exactly `auth.uid` (using `.get('selfElectedSupervisors', [])` to handle missing-field on first add).
- [firestore.rules:551](firestore.rules:551) — `workspaces` update rule now allows owner OR the self-toggle.

**Status doc:** flipped G1 + G2 to ✅ DONE in [PROJECT_OVERVIEW.md](PROJECT_OVERVIEW.md), updated the live-data audit, added a prominent deploy note.

## One critical manual step before this works in prod

The Firestore rules change is **staged but not deployed**. Until you run:

```
firebase deploy --only firestore:rules
```

…the self-toggle UI will hit `permission-denied`. Everything else (the live hub, the role chip) works against the existing rules.

## Suggested smoke test once rules are deployed

1. Sign in as a non-teacher student account → workspace card shows "You: member", no toggle.
2. Sign in as a teacher account (`crewProfiles/{uid}.isTeacher === true` or `profileType === 'teacher'`) added to that same workspace → see "Act as supervisor" button. Click it → role chip flips to "You: supervisor (self)".
3. Try to delete or update a screenplay in that workspace as the now-supervisor → should fail with permission denied (the `canEditScreenplayData` rule already excludes self-elected supervisors).
4. Click "Step down" → role chip reverts.
5. Open two browsers as different members of the same workspace; add a screenplay in one → it appears in the other within ~1s without reload.

Want me to keep going with G4 + G3 next (annotation provenance + comment-count badges), or pause here for you to deploy + smoke test?

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-27 20:14:48Z)**_

G3 + G4 done. Typecheck clean.

## What changed

**G4 — annotation provenance (in viewer):**
- New state `screenplayWorkspaceId`. Loaded once on mount via `getDoc(screenplays/{id})`.
- New helper `resolveSupervisorAtAuthorTime()` — reads `workspaces/{id}` at write time and returns `true` if the current user is in `supervisorIds` OR `selfElectedSupervisors`. One extra read per annotation write.
- `addAnnotation` and `addTag` now write `supervisorAtAuthorTime: boolean`. The annotation toast distinguishes "Supervisor note added" from a regular annotation.
- `Annotation` and `Tag` interfaces gained the optional `supervisorAtAuthorTime` field.

**G3 — comment-count badges (in hub):**
- New state `unresolvedCountByScreenplay` and `unresolvedFromTeacherCountByScreenplay`.
- New `onSnapshot` effect subscribed to `screenplayAnnotations where screenplayId in [...]` (chunked by 10). On any change, recomputes both maps from accumulated subscription results.
- Each screenplay row now shows two pills: **💬 N** (any unresolved) and **🎓 N** (unresolved from a supervisor — only renders if > 0). Tooltips explain meaning.

**G3 — filter chips + supervisor badge (in viewer):**
- New state `statusFilter: 'open' | 'mine' | 'from_teacher' | 'all'`.
- Chip row above the annotation list with live counts on each chip: `Open (N) · Mine (N) · From teacher (N) · All (N)`. Active chip is solid blue.
- Annotations list now filtered by chip selection.
- Each annotation header gets a small **🎓 supervisor** pill if `supervisorAtAuthorTime === true`. The annotation-item also gets a `from-supervisor` className so you can add a left border in SCSS later if you want a stronger visual.

## Smoke test (full G1→G4 flow)

The full sequence is in [PROJECT_OVERVIEW.md](PROJECT_OVERVIEW.md) under the pick-up pointer. Short version:
1. Open the hub as a member — workspace rows now show 💬 / 🎓 counts (zero if no annotations yet).
2. Open a screenplay → annotation panel has the new chips, defaults to "Open."
3. Toggle yourself supervisor (needs the rules deploy), add an annotation → chip and row both show 🎓 1.
4. Toggle back to member, add another → only 💬 increments.
5. Resolve the supervisor annotation → 🎓 0, 💬 1.

## Next planned step

Per the pick-up pointer: **G6 in-app notifications** when a supervisor comments — red dot on the user menu, optional email. Reuses the `users/{uid}/notifications` pattern. Need to confirm `NotificationCenter.tsx`'s shape first. Then **G7** (drag-and-drop multi-upload + first-run empty state) is a small satisfying win after that.

Doc is up to date. Want me to keep going with G6, or pause here to commit + smoke test?

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-27 20:26:11Z)**_

Annotation flow hardened. Typecheck clean.

## Audit findings → fixes shipped

| # | Bug | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| **S1** | **Subscription leak (critical).** `startRealTimeSync` returned a cleanup function but the mount effect threw it away. Listeners stacked on every open/close. | Capture and call the cleanup on unmount. |
| **S2** | **Silent save failure (critical).** Clicking the PDF area while composing an annotation would call `handleTextSelection`, find an empty selection, and clear `selectionPage` — Save then early-returned with no feedback. | `popupTypeRef` guards the clearing path while a popup is open. Added `selection.rangeCount === 0` guard. |
| **S3** | **Overlay click-eater.** Annotation/tag overlay rectangles caught clicks meant for the PDF text layer — you couldn't select text under an existing comment. | Overlay `pointerEvents: 'none'`; marker icon retains `pointerEvents: 'auto'` and the click handler. |
| **S4** | **Wrong virtualization math.** Hardcoded `pageHeight = 900` while real pages render ~1056px at scale 1.2 → wrong pages loaded/unloaded on scroll. | Live-measured `measuredPageHeight` from the first rendered Page's `offsetHeight`. |
| **S5** | **Scroll jump on visibility toggle.** Placeholder was 900px, real page ~1056px — scroll position shifted when pages crossed the visibility boundary. | Both placeholder and `page-container` `minHeight` use `measuredPageHeight`. Identical reserved space. |
| **S6** | **Falsy-0 fallback** in position calc — selecting at the left edge of a page produced wrong x coordinates. | `\|\|` → `??`. |
| **S7** | **Popup overflow.** Popup placed once at selection time; switching from the choice card to the textarea (twice as tall) could push it off the viewport. | `useEffect` on `popupType` re-runs `calculatePopupPosition` with the actual content height. |
| **S8** | **Redundant one-shot loaders.** `loadAnnotations()` and `loadTags()` ran `getDocs` right before the `onSnapshot` listeners — brief race, dead code. | Removed both. `onSnapshot` is the only source of truth. |

Plus:
- **Optimistic resolve** — clicking "Resolve" flips the UI immediately, rolls back if the write fails.
- **Supervisor markers** — annotations created while in supervisor mode render as 🎓 amber on the PDF (instead of 💬 red). Visual signal on the page itself, not just the side panel.

## Smoke-test plan in [PROJECT_OVERVIEW.md](PROJECT_OVERVIEW.md)

10 concrete steps mapped to each fix — open in two browsers, fast-scroll a 30-page PDF, select text under an existing overlay, etc. The doc's "Where we are right now" section is the resume cue.

## What I deliberately did NOT touch

- `attachSelectionHandlers` re-runs on every page load with a 100ms timeout. Wasteful but benign because of the `removeEventListener` before each add. Worth tidying later via event delegation on the scroll container.
- The per-page overlay rendering loop still re-creates DOM nodes on every annotation change. Could memoize but micro-optimization.
- The drawing-canvas overlay (a separate unused feature) is still in the tree. Untouched.

## What to do next

Smoke-test the 10 cases — the most likely surprises are around the optimistic-resolve rollback path (rare in normal use) and the `measuredPageHeight` settling on the right value at high zoom. If anything feels off, the audit + fixes are documented case-by-case in the doc so it's easy to revert or refine one at a time.

After that confirms smooth, the next forward step is G6 (notifications) so students know when you've commented without checking. Want me to proceed with that, or are you going to smoke-test the annotation pass first?

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-27 20:37:06Z)**_

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-27 20:37:08Z)**_

That's a coordinate-space mismatch. We capture the selection's position relative to `.react-pdf__Page` (the inner page element), but render the overlay relative to `.page-container` (which is wider — it has `display: flex; justify-content: center` so the page is centered inside it with whitespace on either side). So `50%` of the container ≠ `50%` of the page, and the overlay drifts left by half the gutter.

Fix: wrap the Page + its overlays in an `inline-block` div that shrinks to the page's actual size — then `%` positions inside it line up with the page.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-27 20:38:38Z)**_

Fixed. Two things shipped:

**The main bug (S10):**
- Selection capture was relative to `.react-pdf__Page`.
- Overlays were rendered as `%` of `.page-container`.
- The container is `display: flex; justify-content: center`, so the page is centered with whitespace gutters on each side — making the container wider than the page.
- `50% of container` therefore landed half-a-gutter to the left of `50% of page`, explaining the highlight wrapping the word before the actual selection.

**Fix:** wrapped `<Page>` + its overlays in a `<div className="page-frame">` with `position: relative; display: inline-block`. Inline-block shrinks the wrapper to the page's natural size, so percentages inside it equal percentages of the page itself. The `.page-container` still centers everything via flex. The overlay now hugs the selected word exactly.

**Bonus fix (same edit):** `isSingleLine` heuristic was using a hardcoded `pagePixelHeight = 900` to decide whether to apply the vertical-pad/marker-offset adjustment — same out-of-date guess as S4. Swapped to `measuredPageHeight` so it tracks the actual rendered page.

Typecheck clean. Logged as S10 in [PROJECT_OVERVIEW.md](PROJECT_OVERVIEW.md).

Reload and re-test: select a single word like "bolsa" → the highlight box should hug that word exactly, marker right above it.

## i18n pass — main collaboration flow now bilingual

**New translation keys** in both `en` and `es` JSONs (verified to parse):
- `collaboration.*`: `personalNoWorkspace`, `uploadToWorkspace`, `uploadHelp`, `inviteMembersOptional`, `noScreenplaysYet`, `onlyCreatorCanInvite`, plus full `supervisor.*` block (`actAs`, `stepDown`, `enabled`/`disabled`/`toggleError`, `yourRole`/`selfTag`/tooltips), `roles.*` block (member/supervisor/viewer + descriptions), `badges.*` block with pluralization (`_one` / `_other`).
- `screenplay.*`: `popupHeader.dragToMove`, `supervisorBadge.{label,tooltip}`, `marker.{annotation,supervisorNote,tag}` (interpolated with `{{user}}` / `{{content}}`), `toasts.*` (add/resolve/reopen/fail variants), `statusFilters.*` with `{{count}}`, full `export.*` block (button labels, column headers, type/boolean values).

**Both components updated**:
- [CollaborationHub.tsx](src/components/Collaboration/CollaborationHub.tsx) — every G1/G3 hardcoded string replaced with `t()`. `INVITABLE_WORKSPACE_ROLES` is now just `[{value: 'member'}, ...]`; labels and descriptions resolve via `t('collaboration.roles.<value>')` at render time so the dropdown stays in the active language without a constant rebuild.
- [ScreenplayViewer.tsx](src/components/Collaboration/ScreenplayViewer.tsx) — filter chips, supervisor badge, marker tooltips, popup-header title, all toasts.

**Language detection already works** — `src/i18n.ts` uses `i18next-browser-languagedetector` looking at `?lang=`, `localStorage`, and `navigator.language`. Spanish students get Spanish automatically.

## CSV report export

New **"⬇ Export"** button at the top of the viewer's annotation side panel, next to the "💬 Annotations (N)" heading. It calls `exportTagReport()` which:

- Combines **annotations + tags** into one report.
- Columns (localized headers): Type · Category · Page · Content · Author · Supervisor · Resolved · Timestamp · Screenplay.
- Boolean values render as localized "Yes"/"No" / "Sí"/"No".
- Tag categories rendered via the existing `screenplay.categories.<key>` translations (30+ production categories already translated).
- Rows sorted by page ascending, then timestamp.
- **UTF-8 BOM** prefix so Excel opens accented characters correctly. CRLF line endings.
- Proper CSV escaping: every cell wrapped in `"`, internal `"` doubled — handles commas, line breaks, semicolons in annotation content without breakage.
- Filename: `<screenplay-slug>-breakdown-<YYYY-MM-DD>.csv`.
- Empty state: toast "Nothing to export yet" if no tags or annotations exist.
- Implementation is plain `Blob` + anchor-click download. No new dependencies.

Use cases: instructor exports a student's annotated screenplay for review/grading; script supervisor exports the breakdown CSV for the AD/production team.

## Smoke-test sequence for this pass

1. Set browser language to Spanish (or visit `?lang=es`) — reload the collaboration page. Workspace labels, role chip, "Act as supervisor" button, status filter chips, supervisor badge, marker tooltips all in Spanish.
2. Open a screenplay with at least one tag + one annotation → click "⬇ Export". A CSV downloads with localized headers ("Tipo, Categoría, Página…").
3. Open the CSV in Excel — accented characters (ñ, é, ó) render correctly thanks to the BOM.
4. Switch back to English, repeat export — headers are English ("Type, Category, Page…"), categories like "Cast Member" instead of "Miembro del Reparto".

Commit 1: collaboration + screenplay evolution

```bash
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Collaboration hub: persist workspaces, supervisor role, live updates, annotation UX, CSV export, i18n

Workspace model
- Persist all workspace + screenplay state to Firestore (prior in-memory bug
  meant new workspaces vanished on reload).
- Live updates: onSnapshot drives the workspaces list, the screenplays list,
  and per-screenplay annotation counts. New uploads + comments appear without
  reload across browsers.
- Roles: WorkspaceMember.role union now includes supervisor (read + comment +
  annotate, no edit). Owner-assigned at invite, OR self-promoted by anyone
  with isTeacher === true on their crew profile. Self-elected supervisors
  tracked in workspaces.selfElectedSupervisors[].
- Firestore rules: workspaces split into get/list/create/update/delete;
  screenplays gain canEditScreenplayData + keepsScreenplayOwnership so a
  supervisor cannot mutate students' screenplays from the rules layer (not
  just UI). New helpers profileIsTeacher + isSelfSupervisorToggle permit the
  narrow self-toggle write.

Screenplay viewer hardening (the comment/tag/annotate flow)
- Capture the onSnapshot cleanup from startRealTimeSync (was discarded; led
  to subscription stacking across viewer opens).
- Don't clear selectionPage on PDF clicks while the annotation popup is open
  (was silently breaking Save).
- Overlay rectangles are pointer-events: none; only the marker icon is
  clickable, so text selection works under existing annotations/tags.
- Measure rendered page height from the first page; use it for both the
  virtualization math and the placeholder reservation. No more scroll jump
  when pages cross the visibility boundary, no more wrong-pages-loaded at
  non-default zoom.
- Wrap Page + overlays in an inline-block .page-frame so the overlay's %
  coordinates refer to the page itself, not the wider centered container.
  Fixes the "highlight wraps the word BEFORE the selection" drift.
- Popup drag handler moved to the header (with a drag-handle glyph and
  cursor: grab), leaving the body inert so the tag-type select, text input,
  Save, and Cancel buttons all click normally instead of dragging the popup.
- Popup reposition on type change so the textarea variant doesn't overflow
  the viewport.
- ?? over || in position fallback so a selection at the left page edge
  doesn't render at window-relative coords.
- Optimistic resolve toggle: UI flips instantly, rolls back on write failure.

Comment-count + supervisor provenance
- Annotations and tags written while acting as a supervisor carry a
  denormalized supervisorAtAuthorTime boolean.
- Hub rows show two pills per screenplay: unresolved-count and
  unresolved-from-supervisor count, driven by a chunked onSnapshot over
  screenplayAnnotations.
- Viewer annotation panel: filter chips (Open / Mine / From teacher / All)
  with live counts; supervisor-authored items also marked with a 🎓 amber
  pill on the page marker and in the side-panel header.

i18n
- All collaboration + screenplay strings touched in this commit go through
  t(). New keys added in both en and es translation JSONs: supervisor.*,
  roles.*, badges.* with i18next pluralization, statusFilters.*,
  supervisorBadge.*, marker.*, toasts.*, popupHeader.*, export.*.
- INVITABLE_WORKSPACE_ROLES is now just a value list; labels resolve via
  t('collaboration.roles.<value>') at render time.

Tag/annotation CSV export
- New "Export report" button at the top of the viewer's annotation panel.
- Combines annotations + tags into one report with columns: Type, Category,
  Page, Content, Author, Supervisor, Resolved, Timestamp, Screenplay.
  Headers and Yes/No values localized. Tag categories rendered via
  screenplay.categories.* (already translated across 30 production categories).
- UTF-8 with BOM so Excel opens accented characters correctly; CRLF; proper
  CSV escaping (every cell quoted, internal " doubled).
- Filename: <screenplay-slug>-breakdown-<YYYY-MM-DD>.csv.

Manual follow-up (NOT automated here)
- firebase deploy --only firestore:rules
  Required to activate isSelfSupervisorToggle / profileIsTeacher and the
  widened workspaces update rule. Without this deploy, the "Act as
  supervisor" toggle hits permission-denied. The rest of the hub already
  works against existing rules.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)" && git status
```

```text
const FIREBASE_STORAGE_MEDIA_BASE = 'https://firebasestorage.googleapis.com/v0/b';

function buildFirebaseStorageMediaUrl(bucket: string, storagePath: string): string {
  return `${FIREBASE_STORAGE_MEDIA_BASE}/${encodeURIComponent(bucket)}/o/${encodeURIComponent(storagePath)}?alt=media`;
}

export function resolveProjectImageUrl(rawUrl?: string | null): string | null {
  const url = typeof rawUrl === 'string' ? rawUrl.trim() : '';

  if (!url || url.startsWith('blob:')) {
    return null;
  }

  if (url.startsWith('//')) {
    return `https:${url}`;
  }

  if (/^(https?:|data:image\/|\/)/i.test(url)) {
    return url;
  }

  if (url.startsWith('gs://')) {
    const storageReference = url.slice('gs://'.length);
    const firstSlashIndex = storageReference.indexOf('/');

    if (firstSlashIndex <= 0) {
      return null;
    }

    const bucket = storageReference.slice(0, firstSlashIndex);
    const storagePath = storageReference.slice(firstSlashIndex + 1);
    return buildFirebaseStorageMediaUrl(bucket, storagePath);
  }

  const bucket = process.env.REACT_APP_FIREBASE_STORAGE_BUCKET;
  if (bucket && /^[\w./% -]+$/.test(url)) {
    return buildFirebaseStorageMediaUrl(bucket, url);
  }

  return null;
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-27 22:07:16Z)**_

Two things shipped + plan refreshed.

## C1 — "Unknown" collaborator bug — fixed

**Root cause:** `screenplays.teamMembers` was being populated by two write paths with incompatible shapes:
- `CollaborationHub.syncWorkspaceScreenplayAccess` writes **uid strings** (correct — matches the Firestore rule `teamMembers.hasAny([request.auth.uid])`).
- Legacy `ScreenplayViewer.addCollaborator` wrote **rich objects** `{id, name, email, ...}`.

The collaborator listener pulled the array and rendered each entry as `user.name || 'Unknown'` — uid-string entries had no `.name`, so every workspace-synced member showed as "Unknown". After you deleted + re-uploaded a screenplay, only the workspace-sync path populated `teamMembers` → all "Unknown".

**Fix in [ScreenplayViewer.tsx](src/components/Collaboration/ScreenplayViewer.tsx):**

- **Listener** now normalizes each entry to a uid (handles both shapes), batch-fetches `crewProfiles` in chunks of 10, shapes into `{id, name, email, avatar, role}` for the UI. Missing crew profiles fall back to `Crew Member XXXX` (last 4 chars of the uid) — never "Unknown". Guarded against stale async with a `requestToken` counter (newer snapshots supersede in-flight hydration).
- **`addCollaborator`** now writes `arrayUnion(user.id)` — uid string only — so future writes match the rule + the workspace-sync shape. Optimistic local update still surfaces the rich profile instantly; listener reconciles within ~1s.
- Old data with object entries keeps working — listener handles both shapes, no migration needed.

Reload your viewer, the workspace-synced member should show with their real name now.

## Fountain editor — still on the roadmap, now resurfaced

You're right that workstream B (the in-browser Fountain screenplay writer) has gone quiet while we hardened the PDF flow. I pulled it back into the "Where we are right now" pick-up pointer in [PROJECT_OVERVIEW.md](PROJECT_OVERVIEW.md) with explicit "NOT started" status and a one-line reminder that B4 (the Fountain parser + page-count heuristic) is the highest-risk piece and should be built + unit-tested in isolation first. Full spec is still at B1–B7 in the same doc.

## Working tree state

Two files dirty, not committed yet:
- [PROJECT_OVERVIEW.md](PROJECT_OVERVIEW.md) — new C1 section + the roadmap table
- [src/components/Collaboration/ScreenplayViewer.tsx](src/components/Collaboration/ScreenplayViewer.tsx) — the listener + writer fix

Want me to commit this as a small dedicated C1 fix, or leave it staged for you to test live first?

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-28 02:32:37Z)**_

Good question — bombardment is exactly the failure mode to avoid. The right shape:

**My recommendation for G6: in-app only, no email.** Every supervisor annotation/tag writes one notification doc to the existing `notifications` collection — the user already has a red-dot bell in the header (via `useNotifications` + `NotificationBell`) that picks it up instantly with no email round-trip. Zero spam risk because there's no inbox involved; students see "Francisco left a note on Scene 2" the next time they're on the site (or live if they're already there).

**Email — defer until we have batching.** A per-input email is exactly the bombardment you're worried about. The right design is a once-per-day digest ("Francisco left 5 new notes on your screenplays") via a Cloud Function on a schedule — that's its own workstream (a scheduler + a queryable "new since last digest" cutoff). Not tonight.

**Tradeoffs:**
- In-app only = no friction, but a student who never visits the site doesn't get nudged.
- A future opt-in toggle on the user profile (`emailDigest: 'off' | 'daily' | 'weekly'`) is easy to add once the Cloud Function exists. Off by default.

<tool-use data-tool-type="generic" data-tool-name="AskUserQuestion"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **AskUserQuestion**</summary>
**Which notification path should I build right now?**

Options:
- **In-app only (Recommended)** - One Firestore notification doc per supervisor annotation. Red-dot bell + dropdown entry. No email, zero spam risk. Ships tonight.
- **In-app + 1 email per comment** - Each supervisor comment also sends an email immediately. Bombardment risk — every individual note triggers a separate email.
- **In-app now, email digest later** - Same as in-app only tonight; we add a daily Cloud-Function digest as a separate workstream when ready.
- **Hold off on notifications, do something else first** - Move on to G7 (drag-and-drop + empty state) or B (Fountain editor) instead.


**Answer:** In-app only (Recommended)
</details></tool-use>

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-28 02:42:46Z)**_

G6 shipped: commit `2bc6c7d3`. Working tree clean.

## What landed

**When a supervisor leaves an annotation or tag**, the screenplay's `uploadedBy` user gets one notification doc written to the top-level `notifications` collection. The student's existing red-dot bell + dropdown picks it up instantly via the already-wired `useNotifications` hook — no email, no spam.

**Schema** matches `AppNotification` (the shape `useNotifications` consumes):
- `type`: `supervisor_annotation` or `supervisor_tag`
- `title`: localized — e.g. *"Francisco left a note on Scene 2.pdf"*
- `body`: page + 80-char excerpt — e.g. *"Page 4: \"This dialogue feels rushed…\""*
- `metadata`: carries `screenplayId`, `screenplayName`, `workspaceId`, the annotation/tag id, page number, and kind so downstream filtering has all the keys
- `link`: `/collaboration` so clicking the notification routes somewhere useful

**Guards** so notifications are never noisy or broken:
- Skipped if there's no current user, or if it would be a self-notify (teacher commenting on their own demo), or if the screenplay has no `uploadedBy` (defensive for legacy docs).
- Notification write is fire-and-forget in a try/catch — a notification failure never blocks the underlying comment.

**Also added**:
- `NotificationCenter` knows about the two new types — uses the 🎓 icon and routes to `/collaboration`.
- i18n keys in `en` + `es` for title, body, and fallback author/screenplay names.

## How to test

1. Sign in as a student. Upload a screenplay into a workspace.
2. Sign in as a teacher (in another browser) where your `crewProfiles.isTeacher === true`. Join the workspace. Click **"Act as supervisor"** on your own member chip *(this needs the pending firestore.rules deploy)*.
3. Open the screenplay, select a word, add an annotation.
4. Back on the student's browser → red dot on the notification bell appears within ~1s. Click the bell → see *"<your name> left a note on <screenplay>"* with the page + excerpt.

## What's next on the G-list

With G6 done, the highest-value remaining items are:
- **G7 — drag-and-drop + first-run empty state** (~30 min, satisfying polish)
- **G5 — workspace activity feed** ("X uploaded Y · 3m ago" timeline in the workspace card)
- **B — Fountain editor** (the in-browser screenplay writer — Francisco specifically asked to keep this visible; it's the next *big* feature, not a small one)

Want me to keep going with G7 (quick win) before the bigger workstream B, or jump straight into the Fountain editor?

```typescript
// Simplified Fountain parsing + pagination utility.
//
// This is intentionally a SUBSET of the Fountain spec (https://fountain.io) — enough to
// classify screenplay elements for rendering, drive the editor's format toolbar/shortcuts,
// and produce a running page count. It does NOT render visual page breaks (per product
// decision); it only estimates the page number a writer has reached.
//
// Pure module: no React, no Firebase. Fully unit-tested in fountain.test.ts.

export type ScreenplayElementType =
  | 'scene_heading'
  | 'action'
  | 'character'
  | 'parenthetical'
  | 'dialogue'
  | 'transition';

export interface ParsedElement {
  type: ScreenplayElementType;
  text: string;
  /** 0-based index of the source line where this element appears. */
  lineIndex: number;
}

const SCENE_PREFIXES = ['INT./EXT.', 'INT/EXT.', 'I/E.', 'INT.', 'EXT.', 'EST.'];

// Per-element character widths used by the page-count heuristic. Roughly matches
// standard screenplay margins: action runs full width, dialogue is indented both sides,
// character/parenthetical narrower still.
const ELEMENT_WIDTHS: Record<ScreenplayElementType, number> = {
  scene_heading: 60,
  action: 60,
  character: 38,
  parenthetical: 25,
  dialogue: 35,
  transition: 60
};

// Standard screenplay page ≈ 55 lines of text at standard margins.
export const LINES_PER_PAGE = 55;

// Tab cycles element types in this order (matches Final Draft / Highland muscle memory).
const TAB_CYCLE: ScreenplayElementType[] = [
  'action',
  'character',
  'dialogue',
  'parenthetical',
  'transition',
  'scene_heading'
];

function normalize(source: string): string {
  return source.replace(/\r\n/g, '\n').replace(/\r/g, '\n');
}

export function isSceneHeading(line: string): boolean {
  const trimmed = line.trim();
  if (!trimmed) return false;
  // Forced scene heading: a leading single dot (but not "..", which is a forced action).
  if (trimmed.startsWith('.') && !trimmed.startsWith('..')) return true;
  const upper = trimmed.toUpperCase();
  return SCENE_PREFIXES.some(prefix => upper.startsWith(prefix));
}

export function isTransition(line: string): boolean {
  const trimmed = line.trim();
  if (!trimmed) return false;
  // Forced transition: leading ">" (and not the centered-text ">...<" form).
  if (trimmed.startsWith('>') && !trimmed.endsWith('<')) return true;
  if (trimmed !== trimmed.toUpperCase()) return false; // transitions are all caps
  if (isSceneHeading(trimmed)) return false;
  return /\bTO:$/.test(trimmed);
}

export function isParenthetical(line: string): boolean {
  const trimmed = line.trim();
  return trimmed.startsWith('(') && trimmed.endsWith(')') && trimmed.length >= 2;
}

export function isCharacter(line: string, nextLine: string | undefined): boolean {
  const trimmed = line.trim();
  if (!trimmed) return false;
  // Forced character cue: leading "@".
  if (trimmed.startsWith('@')) return true;
  if (trimmed !== trimmed.toUpperCase()) return false; // character cues are all caps
  if (!/[A-Z]/.test(trimmed)) return false; // must contain at least one letter
  if (isSceneHeading(trimmed) || isTransition(trimmed)) return false;
  // A character cue is followed by dialogue (a non-blank line).
  return Boolean(nextLine && nextLine.trim() !== '');
}

/**
 * Parse Fountain source into a flat list of typed elements. Blank lines produce no
 * element (they are structural separators), but their effect on pagination is handled
 * in computePageCount.
 */
export function parseFountain(source: string): ParsedElement[] {
  const lines = normalize(source).split('\n');
  const elements: ParsedElement[] = [];
  let inDialogueBlock = false;

  for (let i = 0; i < lines.length; i++) {
    const line = lines[i];
    const trimmed = line.trim();

    if (trimmed === '') {
      inDialogueBlock = false;
      continue;
    }

    const next = lines[i + 1];

    if (isSceneHeading(line)) {
      elements.push({ type: 'scene_heading', text: trimmed, lineIndex: i });
      inDialogueBlock = false;
    } else if (isTransition(line)) {
      elements.push({ type: 'transition', text: trimmed, lineIndex: i });
      inDialogueBlock = false;
    } else if (isCharacter(line, next)) {
      elements.push({ type: 'character', text: trimmed, lineIndex: i });
      inDialogueBlock = true;
    } else if (inDialogueBlock && isParenthetical(line)) {
      elements.push({ type: 'parenthetical', text: trimmed, lineIndex: i });
    } else if (inDialogueBlock) {
      elements.push({ type: 'dialogue', text: trimmed, lineIndex: i });
    } else {
      elements.push({ type: 'action', text: trimmed, lineIndex: i });
    }
  }

  return elements;
}

/**
 * Estimate how many pages the source fills. Heuristic, not a true layout engine:
 *  - each element wraps at an element-specific character width
 *  - a blank line is reserved before each scene heading and character cue
 *  - 55 wrapped lines ≈ 1 page
 */
export function computePageCount(source: string): number {
  const elements = parseFountain(source);
  if (elements.length === 0) return 1;

  let totalLines = 0;
  let prevType: ScreenplayElementType | null = null;

  for (const element of elements) {
    if ((element.type === 'scene_heading' || element.type === 'character') && prevType !== null) {
      totalLines += 1; // blank-line separator before the block
    }
    const width = ELEMENT_WIDTHS[element.type];
    const stripped = element.text.replace(/^[.>@]/, '');
    const wrapped = Math.max(1, Math.ceil(stripped.length / width));
    totalLines += wrapped;
    prevType = element.type;
  }

  return Math.max(1, Math.ceil(totalLines / LINES_PER_PAGE));
}

export interface LineBounds {
  start: number;
  end: number;
  line: string;
}

/** Bounds of the line containing `caret` in the (normalized) source. */
export function getCurrentLineBounds(source: string, caret: number): LineBounds {
  const normalized = normalize(source);
  const clamped = Math.max(0, Math.min(caret, normalized.length));
  const start = normalized.lastIndexOf('\n', clamped - 1) + 1;
  let end = normalized.indexOf('\n', clamped);
  if (end === -1) end = normalized.length;
  return { start, end, line: normalized.slice(start, end) };
}

/** Classify the line the caret is currently on. Empty lines default to 'action'. */
export function detectLineType(source: string, caret: number): ScreenplayElementType {
  const normalized = normalize(source);
  const clamped = Math.max(0, Math.min(caret, normalized.length));
  const lineIndex = (normalized.slice(0, clamped).match(/\n/g) || []).length;
  const elements = parseFountain(normalized);
  const match = elements.find(element => element.lineIndex === lineIndex);
  return match ? match.type : 'action';
}

/**
 * Transform the line the caret is on into the given element type, returning new source
 * and a sensible new caret position. Pure line-level transform — does NOT insert blank
 * lines (the editor handles spacing on Enter), so the result is deterministic + testable.
 */
export function applyElementType(
  source: string,
  caret: number,
  type: ScreenplayElementType
): { source: string; caret: number } {
  const normalized = normalize(source);
  const { start, end, line } = getCurrentLineBounds(normalized, caret);
  const content = line.trim();
  let newLine: string;
  let caretInLine: number;

  switch (type) {
    case 'scene_heading': {
      const body = content.replace(/^(INT\.\/EXT\.|INT\/EXT\.|I\/E\.|INT\.|EXT\.|EST\.|\.)\s*/i, '');
      newLine = `INT. ${body.toUpperCase()}`;
      caretInLine = newLine.length;
      break;
    }
    case 'character': {
      newLine = content.replace(/^@/, '').toUpperCase();
      caretInLine = newLine.length;
      break;
    }
    case 'transition': {
      const body = content.replace(/^>/, '').toUpperCase().replace(/\s*TO:$/, '').trim();
      newLine = body ? `${body} TO:` : 'CUT TO:';
      caretInLine = newLine.length;
      break;
    }
    case 'parenthetical': {
      const inner = content.replace(/^\(/, '').replace(/\)$/, '');
      newLine = `(${inner})`;
      caretInLine = newLine.length - 1; // park caret just inside the closing paren
      break;
    }
    case 'dialogue':
    case 'action':
    default: {
      // Plain text: strip any forced-element marker, keep the author's casing.
      newLine = content.replace(/^[.>@]/, '');
      caretInLine = newLine.length;
      break;
    }
  }

  const newSource = normalized.slice(0, start) + newLine + normalized.slice(end);
  return { source: newSource, caret: start + Math.min(caretInLine, newLine.length) };
}

export function nextElementType(current: ScreenplayElementType): ScreenplayElementType {
  const index = TAB_CYCLE.indexOf(current);
  if (index === -1) return TAB_CYCLE[0];
  return TAB_CYCLE[(index + 1) % TAB_CYCLE.length];
}

export function prevElementType(current: ScreenplayElementType): ScreenplayElementType {
  const index = TAB_CYCLE.indexOf(current);
  if (index === -1) return TAB_CYCLE[TAB_CYCLE.length - 1];
  return TAB_CYCLE[(index - 1 + TAB_CYCLE.length) % TAB_CYCLE.length];
}
```

```typescript
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import {
  parseFountain,
  computePageCount,
  applyElementType,
  detectLineType,
  nextElementType,
  prevElementType,
  isSceneHeading,
  isTransition,
  isCharacter,
  isParenthetical,
  LINES_PER_PAGE
} from './fountain';

describe('element predicates', () => {
  it('recognizes scene headings', () => {
    expect(isSceneHeading('INT. KITCHEN - DAY')).toBe(true);
    expect(isSceneHeading('EXT. BEACH - NIGHT')).toBe(true);
    expect(isSceneHeading('EST. CITY SKYLINE')).toBe(true);
    expect(isSceneHeading('INT./EXT. CAR - DAY')).toBe(true);
    expect(isSceneHeading('.FORCED HEADING')).toBe(true); // forced via leading dot
    expect(isSceneHeading('..not a heading')).toBe(false); // double dot = forced action
    expect(isSceneHeading('She walks in.')).toBe(false);
  });

  it('recognizes transitions', () => {
    expect(isTransition('CUT TO:')).toBe(true);
    expect(isTransition('SMASH CUT TO:')).toBe(true);
    expect(isTransition('> Fade to black')).toBe(true); // forced
    expect(isTransition('cut to:')).toBe(false); // not all caps
    expect(isTransition('INT. ROOM - DAY')).toBe(false); // scene heading wins
  });

  it('recognizes parentheticals', () => {
    expect(isParenthetical('(beat)')).toBe(true);
    expect(isParenthetical('(to herself)')).toBe(true);
    expect(isParenthetical('not parenthetical')).toBe(false);
  });

  it('recognizes character cues only when followed by dialogue', () => {
    expect(isCharacter('DANIELA', 'No mucho en verdad.')).toBe(true);
    expect(isCharacter('DANIELA (O.S.)', 'Hello.')).toBe(true);
    expect(isCharacter('@mc', 'yo')).toBe(true); // forced
    expect(isCharacter('DANIELA', '')).toBe(false); // no dialogue under it
    expect(isCharacter('daniela', 'hi')).toBe(false); // not all caps
  });
});

describe('parseFountain', () => {
  it('classifies a basic scene', () => {
    const source = [
      'INT. KITCHEN - DAY',
      '',
      'PAUL stirs a pot.',
      '',
      'DANIELA',
      '(in French)',
      'No mucho en verdad.',
      '',
      'CUT TO:'
    ].join('\n');

    const elements = parseFountain(source);
    const types = elements.map(e => e.type);
    expect(types).toEqual([
      'scene_heading',
      'action',
      'character',
      'parenthetical',
      'dialogue',
      'transition'
    ]);
  });

  it('treats a parenthetical with no preceding character as action', () => {
    const source = ['(this is standalone)'].join('\n');
    const elements = parseFountain(source);
    expect(elements[0].type).toBe('action');
  });

  it('keeps multi-line dialogue in the dialogue block', () => {
    const source = [
      'MARIA',
      'First line of dialogue.',
      'Second line still dialogue.'
    ].join('\n');
    const elements = parseFountain(source);
    expect(elements.map(e => e.type)).toEqual(['character', 'dialogue', 'dialogue']);
  });

  it('records correct line indices (skipping blanks)', () => {
    const source = ['INT. ROOM - DAY', '', 'Action here.'].join('\n');
    const elements = parseFountain(source);
    expect(elements[0].lineIndex).toBe(0);
    expect(elements[1].lineIndex).toBe(2);
  });
});

describe('computePageCount', () => {
  it('returns 1 for empty source', () => {
    expect(computePageCount('')).toBe(1);
    expect(computePageCount('   \n  \n')).toBe(1);
  });

  it('returns 1 for a short scene', () => {
    const source = [
      'INT. KITCHEN - DAY',
      '',
      'PAUL stirs a pot.',
      '',
      'DANIELA',
      'No mucho en verdad.'
    ].join('\n');
    expect(computePageCount(source)).toBe(1);
  });

  it('grows roughly one page per ~55 lines of action', () => {
    // 110 single-line action paragraphs (each < 60 chars => 1 wrapped line),
    // separated by blanks. ~110 lines / 55 ≈ 2 pages.
    const actionLines = Array.from({ length: 110 }, (_, i) => `Action paragraph number ${i}.`);
    const source = actionLines.join('\n\n');
    const pages = computePageCount(source);
    expect(pages).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(2);
    expect(pages).toBeLessThanOrEqual(3);
  });

  it('wraps long action lines into multiple counted lines', () => {
    const longLine = 'x'.repeat(60 * 56); // 56 wrapped lines at width 60 => > 1 page
    expect(computePageCount(longLine)).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(2);
  });

  it('counts dialogue at a narrower width than action', () => {
    // 70-char dialogue wraps to 2 lines (width 35); same text as action wraps to 2 (width 60 => 2).
    const dialogueSource = ['MARIA', 'x'.repeat(70)].join('\n');
    const elements = parseFountain(dialogueSource);
    expect(elements[1].type).toBe('dialogue');
    // Sanity: not zero pages.
    expect(computePageCount(dialogueSource)).toBe(1);
  });
});

describe('applyElementType', () => {
  it('converts a line to a scene heading', () => {
    const source = 'kitchen at night';
    const { source: out, caret } = applyElementType(source, source.length, 'scene_heading');
    expect(out).toBe('INT. KITCHEN AT NIGHT');
    expect(caret).toBe(out.length);
  });

  it('does not double the INT. prefix', () => {
    const source = 'INT. KITCHEN';
    const { source: out } = applyElementType(source, source.length, 'scene_heading');
    expect(out).toBe('INT. KITCHEN');
  });

  it('uppercases a character cue', () => {
    const source = 'daniela';
    const { source: out } = applyElementType(source, source.length, 'character');
    expect(out).toBe('DANIELA');
  });

  it('wraps a line in parentheses and parks caret inside', () => {
    const source = 'beat';
    const { source: out, caret } = applyElementType(source, source.length, 'parenthetical');
    expect(out).toBe('(beat)');
    expect(caret).toBe(out.length - 1);
  });

  it('formats a transition ending in TO:', () => {
    const source = 'smash cut';
    const { source: out } = applyElementType(source, source.length, 'transition');
    expect(out).toBe('SMASH CUT TO:');
  });

  it('only transforms the current line, not the whole document', () => {
    const source = 'INT. ROOM - DAY\nshe enters\nDANIELA';
    const caret = source.indexOf('she enters') + 2; // caret on the middle line
    const { source: out } = applyElementType(source, caret, 'character');
    expect(out).toBe('INT. ROOM - DAY\nSHE ENTERS\nDANIELA');
  });
});

describe('detectLineType', () => {
  it('detects the type of the line under the caret', () => {
    const source = ['INT. ROOM - DAY', '', 'MARIA', 'Hello there.'].join('\n');
    expect(detectLineType(source, 0)).toBe('scene_heading');
    const mariaIdx = source.indexOf('MARIA');
    expect(detectLineType(source, mariaIdx)).toBe('character');
    const dialogueIdx = source.indexOf('Hello');
    expect(detectLineType(source, dialogueIdx)).toBe('dialogue');
  });

  it('defaults empty lines to action', () => {
    const source = 'INT. ROOM - DAY\n\n';
    expect(detectLineType(source, source.length)).toBe('action');
  });
});

describe('element type cycling', () => {
  it('cycles forward and wraps', () => {
    expect(nextElementType('action')).toBe('character');
    expect(nextElementType('scene_heading')).toBe('action'); // wraps
  });

  it('cycles backward and wraps', () => {
    expect(prevElementType('action')).toBe('scene_heading'); // wraps
    expect(prevElementType('character')).toBe('action');
  });
});

describe('constants', () => {
  it('uses 55 lines per page', () => {
    expect(LINES_PER_PAGE).toBe(55);
  });
});
```

```bash
src/utilities/fountain.ts — a standalone, fully-tested subset of Fountain:
- parseFountain(source): classifies each non-blank line into scene_heading /
  action / character / parenthetical / dialogue / transition, tracking the
  dialogue-block context so lines under a character cue become dialogue.
- computePageCount(source): heuristic page estimate. Each element wraps at an
  element-specific width (action 60, dialogue 35, character 38, parenthetical
  25, scene/transition 60); a blank line is reserved before each scene heading
  and character cue; 55 wrapped lines ≈ 1 page. Used for the editor's running
  page badge (no visual page breaks — product decision).
- applyElementType(source, caret, type): pure line-level transform powering the
  format toolbar + keyboard shortcuts (INT. prefix, uppercase character cue,
  ( ) wrap with caret parked inside, "… TO:" transition). Deterministic, only
  touches the current line.
- detectLineType(source, caret): classify the caret's line for active-element
  highlighting + Tab cycling.
- nextElementType / prevElementType: Tab / Shift+Tab cycle order.

fountain.test.ts — 24 Vitest cases covering predicates, parsing (incl. the
"standalone parenthetical = action" and multi-line dialogue edge cases),
page-count bounds, line-scoped transforms, and cycle wrap. All green.

This is B4 from the plan, built + tested in isolation before any editor UI
depends on it (it's the riskiest piece). B1/B2 (schema + creation flow), B3
(editor), B5 (viewer) follow.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"
```

```tsx
import React, { useState, useEffect, useRef, useCallback } from 'react';
import { doc, getDoc, updateDoc, serverTimestamp } from 'firebase/firestore';
import { db } from '../../firebase';
import { useAuth } from '../../contexts/AuthContext';
import { useTranslation } from 'react-i18next';
import { toast } from 'react-hot-toast';
import {
  ScreenplayElementType,
  applyElementType,
  computePageCount,
  detectLineType,
  nextElementType,
  prevElementType
} from '../../utilities/fountain';

interface FountainEditorProps {
  screenplay: { id: string; name: string; fountainSource?: string };
  onClose: () => void;
}

type SaveStatus = 'idle' | 'saving' | 'saved' | 'error';

const SAVE_DEBOUNCE_MS = 1500;

// Toolbar button order + the keyboard letter that triggers each (with Alt/Option).
const TOOLBAR: Array<{ type: ScreenplayElementType; labelKey: string; key: string }> = [
  { type: 'scene_heading', labelKey: 'fountain.elements.scene', key: 'S' },
  { type: 'action', labelKey: 'fountain.elements.action', key: 'A' },
  { type: 'character', labelKey: 'fountain.elements.character', key: 'C' },
  { type: 'parenthetical', labelKey: 'fountain.elements.parenthetical', key: 'P' },
  { type: 'dialogue', labelKey: 'fountain.elements.dialogue', key: 'D' },
  { type: 'transition', labelKey: 'fountain.elements.transition', key: 'T' }
];

const isMac = typeof navigator !== 'undefined' && /Mac|iPhone|iPad/.test(navigator.platform);
const modLabel = isMac ? '⌥' : 'Alt+';

const FountainEditor: React.FC<FountainEditorProps> = ({ screenplay, onClose }) => {
  const { currentUser } = useAuth();
  const { t } = useTranslation();
  const textareaRef = useRef<HTMLTextAreaElement>(null);

  const [source, setSource] = useState(screenplay.fountainSource || '');
  const [saveStatus, setSaveStatus] = useState<SaveStatus>('idle');
  const [activeType, setActiveType] = useState<ScreenplayElementType>('action');

  const saveTimer = useRef<number | null>(null);
  const pendingCaret = useRef<number | null>(null);
  const latestSource = useRef(source);
  latestSource.current = source;

  const pageCount = computePageCount(source);

  // Load the freshest source once on mount (the list-level copy may be stale).
  useEffect(() => {
    let cancelled = false;
    (async () => {
      try {
        const snap = await getDoc(doc(db, 'screenplays', screenplay.id));
        if (cancelled || !snap.exists()) return;
        const data = snap.data();
        if (typeof data.fountainSource === 'string') {
          setSource(data.fountainSource);
        }
      } catch (err) {
        console.error('Failed to load fountain source:', err);
      }
    })();
    return () => {
      cancelled = true;
    };
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, [screenplay.id]);

  // Persist (debounced). Last write wins — no merge, no version (per product decision).
  const scheduleSave = useCallback((value: string) => {
    if (saveTimer.current) {
      window.clearTimeout(saveTimer.current);
    }
    setSaveStatus('saving');
    saveTimer.current = window.setTimeout(async () => {
      try {
        await updateDoc(doc(db, 'screenplays', screenplay.id), {
          fountainSource: value,
          fountainUpdatedAt: serverTimestamp(),
          lastModified: serverTimestamp(),
          lastEditedBy: currentUser?.uid || null
        });
        setSaveStatus('saved');
      } catch (err) {
        console.error('Failed to save fountain source:', err);
        setSaveStatus('error');
        toast.error(t('fountain.saveError'));
      }
    }, SAVE_DEBOUNCE_MS);
  }, [screenplay.id, currentUser?.uid, t]);

  // Flush any pending save on unmount.
  useEffect(() => {
    return () => {
      if (saveTimer.current) {
        window.clearTimeout(saveTimer.current);
        // Best-effort final write so closing immediately after typing doesn't lose work.
        updateDoc(doc(db, 'screenplays', screenplay.id), {
          fountainSource: latestSource.current,
          fountainUpdatedAt: serverTimestamp(),
          lastModified: serverTimestamp(),
          lastEditedBy: currentUser?.uid || null
        }).catch(err => console.error('Final fountain save failed:', err));
      }
    };
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, [screenplay.id]);

  // Restore caret after a programmatic source change (toolbar / shortcut transforms).
  useEffect(() => {
    if (pendingCaret.current != null && textareaRef.current) {
      const pos = pendingCaret.current;
      textareaRef.current.focus();
      textareaRef.current.setSelectionRange(pos, pos);
      pendingCaret.current = null;
    }
  }, [source]);

  const refreshActiveType = useCallback(() => {
    const el = textareaRef.current;
    if (!el) return;
    setActiveType(detectLineType(el.value, el.selectionStart));
  }, []);

  const handleChange = (e: React.ChangeEvent<HTMLTextAreaElement>) => {
    const value = e.target.value;
    setSource(value);
    scheduleSave(value);
    setActiveType(detectLineType(value, e.target.selectionStart));
  };

  const applyType = useCallback((type: ScreenplayElementType) => {
    const el = textareaRef.current;
    if (!el) return;
    const caret = el.selectionStart;
    const result = applyElementType(el.value, caret, type);
    pendingCaret.current = result.caret;
    setSource(result.source);
    scheduleSave(result.source);
    setActiveType(type);
  }, [scheduleSave]);

  const handleKeyDown = (e: React.KeyboardEvent<HTMLTextAreaElement>) => {
    const el = textareaRef.current;
    if (!el) return;

    // Tab / Shift+Tab cycle the current line's element type.
    if (e.key === 'Tab') {
      e.preventDefault();
      const current = detectLineType(el.value, el.selectionStart);
      applyType(e.shiftKey ? prevElementType(current) : nextElementType(current));
      return;
    }

    // Alt/Option + letter -> direct element type. Alt+letter is free inside a focused
    // textarea once we preventDefault, so we "own" these while editing.
    if (e.altKey && !e.ctrlKey && !e.metaKey) {
      const match = TOOLBAR.find(item => item.key.toLowerCase() === e.key.toLowerCase());
      if (match) {
        e.preventDefault();
        applyType(match.type);
        return;
      }
    }
  };

  return (
    <div className="fountain-editor-overlay" style={overlayStyle}>
      <div className="fountain-editor" style={editorStyle}>
        {/* Header */}
        <div style={headerStyle}>
          <div style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 12, minWidth: 0 }}>
            <strong style={{ fontSize: '1.05em', color: '#0f172a', whiteSpace: 'nowrap', overflow: 'hidden', textOverflow: 'ellipsis' }}>
              {screenplay.name}
            </strong>
            <span style={saveBadgeStyle(saveStatus)}>
              {saveStatus === 'saving' && t('fountain.saving')}
              {saveStatus === 'saved' && t('fountain.saved')}
              {saveStatus === 'error' && t('fountain.saveErrorShort')}
              {saveStatus === 'idle' && ''}
            </span>
          </div>
          <div style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 16 }}>
            <span style={pageBadgeStyle} title={t('fountain.pageCountTooltip')}>
              {t('fountain.pageCount', { count: pageCount })}
            </span>
            <button type="button" onClick={onClose} style={closeBtnStyle} aria-label={t('fountain.close')}>×</button>
          </div>
        </div>

        {/* Format toolbar */}
        <div style={toolbarStyle}>
          {TOOLBAR.map(item => {
            const active = activeType === item.type;
            return (
              <button
                key={item.type}
                type="button"
                onClick={() => applyType(item.type)}
                style={toolbarButtonStyle(active)}
                title={`${t(item.labelKey)} — ${item.type === 'scene_heading' ? '⇥ / ' : ''}${modLabel}${item.key}`}
              >
                <span style={{ fontWeight: 600 }}>{t(item.labelKey)}</span>
                <span style={{ fontSize: '0.7em', color: active ? 'rgba(255,255,255,0.85)' : '#94a3b8' }}>
                  {item.type === 'scene_heading' ? `⇥ ${modLabel}${item.key}` : `${modLabel}${item.key}`}
                </span>
              </button>
            );
          })}
        </div>

        {/* Editor body */}
        <textarea
          ref={textareaRef}
          value={source}
          onChange={handleChange}
          onKeyDown={handleKeyDown}
          onClick={refreshActiveType}
          onKeyUp={refreshActiveType}
          placeholder={t('fountain.placeholder')}
          spellCheck
          style={textareaStyle}
        />
      </div>
    </div>
  );
};

const overlayStyle: React.CSSProperties = {
  position: 'fixed',
  inset: 0,
  background: 'rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.55)',
  zIndex: 2500,
  display: 'flex',
  alignItems: 'center',
  justifyContent: 'center',
  padding: 16
};

const editorStyle: React.CSSProperties = {
  background: '#ffffff',
  borderRadius: 12,
  width: 'min(860px, 100%)',
  height: 'min(90vh, 100%)',
  display: 'flex',
  flexDirection: 'column',
  overflow: 'hidden',
  boxShadow: '0 24px 60px rgba(2, 6, 23, 0.45)'
};

const headerStyle: React.CSSProperties = {
  display: 'flex',
  alignItems: 'center',
  justifyContent: 'space-between',
  padding: '12px 18px',
  borderBottom: '1px solid #e2e8f0',
  gap: 12
};

const pageBadgeStyle: React.CSSProperties = {
  background: '#0f172a',
  color: '#fff',
  borderRadius: 999,
  padding: '3px 12px',
  fontSize: '0.85em',
  fontWeight: 700
};

const closeBtnStyle: React.CSSProperties = {
  background: 'none',
  border: 'none',
  fontSize: '1.8rem',
  lineHeight: 1,
  color: '#64748b',
  cursor: 'pointer'
};

const toolbarStyle: React.CSSProperties = {
  display: 'flex',
  gap: 8,
  padding: '10px 18px',
  borderBottom: '1px solid #eef2f7',
  flexWrap: 'wrap',
  background: '#f8fafc'
};

const toolbarButtonStyle = (active: boolean): React.CSSProperties => ({
  display: 'flex',
  flexDirection: 'column',
  alignItems: 'center',
  gap: 2,
  minWidth: 78,
  padding: '6px 8px',
  borderRadius: 8,
  border: `1px solid ${active ? '#2563eb' : '#cbd5e1'}`,
  background: active ? '#2563eb' : '#ffffff',
  color: active ? '#ffffff' : '#1e293b',
  cursor: 'pointer',
  fontSize: '0.85em',
  transition: 'all 0.12s ease'
});

const saveBadgeStyle = (status: SaveStatus): React.CSSProperties => ({
  fontSize: '0.8em',
  color: status === 'error' ? '#b91c1c' : '#64748b',
  whiteSpace: 'nowrap'
});

const textareaStyle: React.CSSProperties = {
  flex: 1,
  width: '100%',
  border: 'none',
  outline: 'none',
  resize: 'none',
  padding: '24px clamp(24px, 8%, 96px)',
  fontFamily: '"Courier Prime", "Courier New", Courier, monospace',
  fontSize: 15,
  lineHeight: 1.5,
  color: '#1e293b',
  background: '#ffffff'
};

export default FountainEditor;
```
